## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Dutiyaaniyata* ("2. Sitting alone with a woman", Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Aniyata 2) constitutes the second of the two undetermined (*aniyata*) disciplinary rules within the *Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga* of the Pali Vinaya Piṭaka [SuttaCentral]. The rule regulates cases where a trustworthy female lay follower observes a Buddhist monk sitting alone in private with a woman; if she charges him with a disciplinary breach that entails either temporary suspension (*saṅghādisesa*) or an offense requiring confession (*pācittiya*), and the monk acknowledges the act, he is dealt with according to whichever category of offense he admits having committed [SuttaCentral]. An English translation of the rule and its exposition has been made by Bhikkhu Brahmali [SuttaCentral].

Curated parallels recorded by SuttaCentral demonstrate that this undetermined rule is shared widely across early Buddhist monastic lineages, appearing in the Prātimokṣa and Vibhaṅga traditions of the Sarvāstivāda, Mūlasarvāstivāda, Mahīśāsaka, Mahāsāṅghika, Dharmaguptaka, Lokottaravāda, and Kāśyapīya schools preserved in Chinese, Sanskrit, and Tibetan [SuttaCentral]. Within the Pali canon, SuttaCentral notes internal parallels in the *Bhikkhu Pātimokkha*, the *Parivāra*, the first undetermined rule (*Aniyata* 1), and several related rules on private association with women (*Pācittiya* 30, 44, and 45) [SuttaCentral]. Computational analysis by DharmaNexus confirms extensive textual overlap between this rule and other Vinaya sections, sharing its largest blocks of formulaic legal phrasings with *Aniyata* 1 (152 matching passages) and the *Pātimokkha*, as well as aligning with Tibetan Vinaya texts including the *Vinayavibhaṅga* and *Vinaya-uttaragrantha* [DharmaNexus].
